lessons.title: Point of View, Connotation & Tone (Part 1 of 2)
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Point of View and Connotation
lessons.reading: First-person narrators use "I." Third-person limited knows one character’s thoughts, while omniscient knows all characters’ thoughts. Connotation is the positive or negative feeling a word carries.

principles.title: Narrative Point of View, Connotation & Tone

bank.passage: Marcus stared at the chessboard, sure his knight would trap Elena’s queen. Across the table, Elena hid a smile because she had seen the trap three turns ago.
bank.prompt: Which point of view is used in this passage?
choices: Third-person omniscient
First-person
Second-person
Stage directions only
bank.answer: Third-person omniscient
bank.explanation: An omniscient narrator is outside the story and knows the thoughts of multiple characters.

bank.prompt: How do the connotations of "thrifty" and "stingy" differ?
choices: "Thrifty" is positive; "stingy" is negative
Both words are harshly negative
"Stingy" is positive; "thrifty" is negative
Neither word has any emotional feeling
bank.answer: "Thrifty" is positive; "stingy" is negative
bank.explanation: Connotation is the positive or negative emotional feeling a word carries beyond its dictionary meaning.

bank.passage: I adjusted my headlamp and stepped into the cool limestone cave. Water dripped from the rock ceiling above me.
bank.prompt: Which point of view is used in this passage?
choices: First-person ("I", "my")
Third-person omniscient
Second-person ("you")
Third-person limited
bank.answer: First-person ("I", "my")
bank.explanation: First-person point of view uses pronouns like "I" and "my" from a character inside the story.

bank.passage: Through three days of freezing sleet, the lighthouse keeper climbed the iron stairs every four hours to keep the warning light shining for ships.
bank.prompt: Which word best describes the author’s tone toward the keeper?
choices: Admiring and respectful
Mocking and rude
Bored and careless
Angry and bitter
bank.answer: Admiring and respectful
bank.explanation: Tone is the author’s attitude toward the subject. Highlighting brave duty creates an admiring tone.

bank.prompt: Which word has the most positive connotation for staying determined?
choices: Persevering
Stubborn
Pigheaded
Obstinate
bank.answer: Persevering
bank.explanation: "Persevering" has a positive connotation of steady courage, while "stubborn" sounds negative.

bank.prompt: What defines a third-person limited narrator?
choices: Shares the inner thoughts of only one character
Uses "I" and "we" to tell the story
Knows every character’s secret thoughts
Gives recipe steps using "you"
bank.answer: Shares the inner thoughts of only one character
bank.explanation: Third-person limited uses "he" or "she" and follows the inner thoughts of just one character.

bank.prompt: Which word has a more positive connotation than "nosy"?
choices: Inquisitive
Prying
Meddling
Snooping
bank.answer: Inquisitive
bank.explanation: "Inquisitive" suggests smart curiosity, whereas "nosy" and "prying" have negative connotations.

bank.prompt: What does it mean to cite textual evidence?
choices: Quote or point to specific details from the text
Guess the ending without reading
Write only your personal feelings
Skip the hard paragraphs
bank.answer: Quote or point to specific details from the text
bank.explanation: Textual evidence is specific facts or quotes from a passage used to prove your analysis.

lessons.title: Evaluating Claims & Evidence (Part 2 of 2)
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Evaluating Arguments and Claims
lessons.reading: A strong argument backs up a debatable claim with verified facts and data rather than personal opinions or bandwagon appeals ("everyone is doing it").

principles.title: Distinguishing Supported Claims from Unverified Opinions
principles.summary: Evaluate whether an author’s claim is supported by credible facts.

bank.prompt: Which evidence best supports starting middle school at 8:30 AM?
choices: A study of 9,000 students showing higher grades
My cousin hates waking up on Mondays
Every cool school is changing its bells
Alarm clocks are very loud
bank.answer: A study of 9,000 students showing higher grades
bank.explanation: Strong arguments rely on verifiable research data rather than personal opinions.

bank.prompt: Which statement is a debatable claim for an argument essay?
choices: Cities should build more protected bike lanes
Bicycles have two wheels and pedals
Columbus is the capital of Ohio
Water freezes at zero degrees Celsius
bank.answer: Cities should build more protected bike lanes
bank.explanation: A claim is a debatable position on an issue that must be proved with evidence.

bank.passage: Buy SolarMax shoes today because millions of fans already wear them!
bank.prompt: Which logical fallacy does this advertisement use?
choices: Bandwagon appeal
Scientific data
Expert medical advice
Historical timeline
bank.answer: Bandwagon appeal
bank.explanation: A bandwagon fallacy claims something is good simply because many other people are doing it.

bank.prompt: Why should an argument essay include a counterclaim?
choices: To address and refute an opposing viewpoint
To confuse the reader about the topic
To prove the author’s own claim is wrong
To avoid using any facts
bank.answer: To address and refute an opposing viewpoint
bank.explanation: A counterclaim is an opposing view. Answering it with evidence makes your argument stronger.

bank.prompt: Which statement gives verifiable factual evidence?
choices: Recycling one ton of aluminum saves 14,000 kWh
Aluminum cans are the prettiest containers
Everyone loves sorting bins on Saturday
Plastic is much more boring than glass
bank.answer: Recycling one ton of aluminum saves 14,000 kWh
bank.explanation: Factual evidence can be measured and checked against reliable records or scientific data.

bank.prompt: What is an ad hominem fallacy in an argument?
choices: Attacking a person instead of their evidence
Using a chart from a science lab
Quoting a dictionary definition
Explaining cause and effect
bank.answer: Attacking a person instead of their evidence
bank.explanation: An ad hominem fallacy attacks the speaker’s character instead of answering their reasoning.

bank.prompt: Which source is most credible for a Lake Erie water report?
choices: Water quality data from the Ohio EPA
An anonymous social media rumour
A comic book about sea monsters
A television commercial for soda
bank.answer: Water quality data from the Ohio EPA
bank.explanation: A credible source is trustworthy and backed by scientific measurement or expert research.

bank.prompt: What connects a piece of evidence back to the author’s claim?
choices: Reasoning
Punctuation
Alliteration
Rhyme
bank.answer: Reasoning
bank.explanation: Reasoning explains how and why the facts prove the author’s main claim.

units.title: Unit 2: Ohio Nonfiction Comparisons, Roots & Pronoun Case

lessons.title: Ohio Nonfiction: Comparing Two Authors (Part 1 of 2)
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Comparing Two Accounts of an Event (OH.RI.6.9)
lessons.reading: Under Ohio Standard OH.RI.6.9, we compare how two authors present the same historical event—such as a personal diary from the 1913 Dayton Flood versus an engineering report.

principles.title: Comparing Two Authors’ Presentations of the Same Event
principles.summary: Compare memoirs, biographies, and technical reports on Ohio and regional events.

bank.passage: Author A writes a diary entry from a family trapped on a roof in the 1913 Dayton Flood. Author B writes an engineering report on Miami River dam costs.
bank.prompt: How do these two authors present the same Ohio event?
choices: Author A shares personal feelings; Author B gives technical data
Both authors write fictional fairy tales
Author A lists dam costs; Author B writes poetry
Neither author mentions the river flood
bank.answer: Author A shares personal feelings; Author B gives technical data
bank.explanation: Different authors can cover the same event using a personal memoir or an objective technical report.

bank.passage: Article 1 celebrates how the Ohio & Erie Canal lowered grain shipping prices. Article 2 focuses on the hard labor and illnesses of canal diggers.
bank.prompt: Why do these two articles emphasize different facts?
choices: Article 1 focuses on trade; Article 2 focuses on workers
Article 1 is about space travel
Both articles ignore the canal completely
Article 2 says canals were never built
bank.answer: Article 1 focuses on trade; Article 2 focuses on workers
bank.explanation: Authors select facts that match their purpose, such as economic growth versus worker conditions.

bank.prompt: What is a memoir compared to a history encyclopedia entry?
choices: A firsthand personal memory of events
A list of state capitals in order
A fictional story about talking animals
A math formula for area
bank.answer: A firsthand personal memory of events
bank.explanation: A memoir is a firsthand account written from personal memory, while an encyclopedia is a summary.

bank.passage: Writer 1 describes Wilbur and Orville Wright’s bicycle shop tools in Dayton. Writer 2 describes the wind speeds on the beach at Kitty Hawk.
bank.prompt: What does comparing both passages help the reader understand?
choices: Both the invention work in Ohio and the flight test
Why bicycles cannot roll on roads
How steamboats cross the ocean
Why the Wright brothers quit flying
bank.answer: Both the invention work in Ohio and the flight test
bank.explanation: Reading multiple accounts gives a fuller picture by combining different stages and details of an event.

bank.prompt: What is an author’s perspective in informational nonfiction?
choices: The viewpoint or angle the author brings to a topic
The font size printed on the book cover
The number of pages in the glossary
The price of the book at a store
bank.answer: The viewpoint or angle the author brings to a topic
bank.explanation: Perspective is the author’s viewpoint, which shapes which facts they highlight or leave out.

bank.prompt: How does an eyewitness letter differ from a textbook chapter?
choices: A letter captures immediate emotion; a textbook gives broad context
A textbook is written before the event happens
An eyewitness letter is always fictional
They are identical in every sentence
bank.answer: A letter captures immediate emotion; a textbook gives broad context
bank.explanation: Primary letters show one witness’s immediate view, while textbooks combine many sources later.

bank.passage: Biographer A highlights Garrett Morgan’s three-position traffic signal invented in Cleveland. Biographer B highlights his safety hood used to rescue tunnel workers.
bank.prompt: What central idea do both biographies support about Garrett Morgan?
choices: His inventions saved lives and improved public safety
He only painted landscapes in Europe
He refused to share any of his ideas
He lived before cities had roads
bank.answer: His inventions saved lives and improved public safety
bank.explanation: Both authors use different examples to show that Garrett Morgan’s inventions protected public safety.

bank.prompt: When two authors disagree on a cause, what should a reader check?
choices: The quality of evidence each author cites
Which book has a shinier cover
Which author has a shorter last name
Only the first sentence of each text
bank.answer: The quality of evidence each author cites
bank.explanation: Comparing two accounts requires checking which author backs up claims with stronger evidence.

lessons.title: Greek/Latin Roots & Pronoun Case (Part 2 of 2)
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Pronoun Case & Greek/Latin Roots
lessons.reading: Roots like "chron" (time), "spect" (look), "port" (carry), and "dict" (say) unlock new words. Use subject pronouns ("I") as subjects and object pronouns ("me") as objects.

principles.title: Greek/Latin Roots and Pronoun Case & Intensive Pronouns
principles.summary: Use Greek/Latin roots and choose correct pronoun cases.

bank.prompt: The Greek root "chron" means time. What does chronological mean?
choices: Arranged in time order from first to last
Organized by brightness of color
Sorted from heaviest to lightest
Written in secret code
bank.answer: Arranged in time order from first to last
bank.explanation: The root "chron" means time, so chronological order arranges events in the order they happened.

bank.prompt: The Latin root "spect" means to look. What does inspect mean?
choices: To look at something closely and carefully
To throw something across a field
To freeze water into ice cubes
To whisper a secret song
bank.answer: To look at something closely and carefully
bank.explanation: Because "spect" means look or see, to inspect is to examine closely.

bank.prompt: Which sentence uses pronoun case correctly?
choices: The coach gave Priya and me the blueprint.
The coach gave Priya and I the blueprint.
Her and me built the robot.
Between you and I, the test was easy.
bank.answer: The coach gave Priya and me the blueprint.
bank.explanation: Use the objective pronoun "me" when it receives the action of the verb ("gave me").

bank.prompt: Which sentence uses an intensive pronoun for emphasis?
choices: The principal herself welded the stage frame.
He accidentally cut himself slicing bread.
They bought tickets for our family.
She handed the microphone to him.
bank.answer: The principal herself welded the stage frame.
bank.explanation: An intensive pronoun (like "herself") adds emphasis to a noun and can be removed without breaking grammar.

bank.prompt: The Latin root "port" means carry. What does portable mean?
choices: Easy to carry from place to place
Too heavy to lift off the ground
Able to glow in the dark
Made entirely out of stone
bank.answer: Easy to carry from place to place
bank.explanation: "Port" means carry and "-able" means capable of, so portable means easy to carry.

bank.prompt: Which revision fixes the vague pronoun in "Leo told Sam he won"?
choices: Leo told Sam that Sam had won.
He told him that he won.
Telling him, he won the prize.
They told him he won it.
bank.answer: Leo told Sam that Sam had won.
bank.explanation: A vague pronoun is unclear about who it refers to. Replacing "he" with "Sam" fixes the confusion.

bank.prompt: The Latin root "dict" means say. What does predict mean?
choices: To say what will happen beforehand
To carry boxes onto a ship
To measure the heat of water
To draw a map of mountains
bank.answer: To say what will happen beforehand
bank.explanation: "Pre-" means before and "dict" means say, so predict means to declare beforehand.

bank.prompt: Which sentence uses the subjective pronoun case correctly?
choices: Ava and I presented our history project.
Ava and me presented our history project.
Him and I studied ancient Egypt.
Me and her read the chapter.
bank.answer: Ava and I presented our history project.
bank.explanation: Use the subjective pronoun "I" when it acts as the subject performing the verb.

bank.prompt: Which point of view is used in this passage?
choices: First-person ("I", "my")
Third-person omniscient
Second-person ("you")
Third-person limited
bank.answer: First-person ("I", "my")
bank.explanation: First-person point of view uses pronouns like "I" and "my" from a character inside the story.

bank.passage: Through three days of freezing sleet, the lighthouse keeper climbed the iron stairs every four hours to keep the warning light shining for ships.
bank.prompt: Which word best describes the author’s tone toward the keeper?
choices: Admiring and respectful
Mocking and rude
Bored and careless
Angry and bitter
bank.answer: Admiring and respectful
bank.explanation: Tone is the author’s attitude toward the subject. Highlighting brave duty creates an admiring tone.

bank.prompt: Which word has the most positive connotation for staying determined?
choices: Persevering
Stubborn
Pigheaded
Obstinate
bank.answer: Persevering
bank.explanation: "Persevering" has a positive connotation of steady courage, while "stubborn" sounds negative.

bank.prompt: What defines a third-person limited narrator?
choices: Shares the inner thoughts of only one character
Uses "I" and "we" to tell the story
Knows every character’s secret thoughts
Gives recipe steps using "you"
bank.answer: Shares the inner thoughts of only one character
bank.explanation: Third-person limited uses "he" or "she" and follows the inner thoughts of just one character.

bank.prompt: Which word has a more positive connotation than "nosy"?
choices: Inquisitive
Prying
Meddling
Snooping
bank.answer: Inquisitive
bank.explanation: "Inquisitive" suggests smart curiosity, whereas "nosy" and "prying" have negative connotations.

bank.prompt: What does it mean to cite textual evidence?
choices: Quote or point to specific details from the text
Guess the ending without reading
Write only your personal feelings
Skip the hard paragraphs
bank.answer: Quote or point to specific details from the text
bank.explanation: Textual evidence is specific facts or quotes from a passage used to prove your analysis.

principles.title: Distinguishing Supported Claims from Unverified Opinions

bank.prompt: Which evidence best supports starting middle school at 8:30 AM?
choices: A study of 9,000 students showing higher grades
My cousin hates waking up on Mondays
Every cool school is changing its bells
Alarm clocks are very loud
bank.answer: A study of 9,000 students showing higher grades
bank.explanation: Strong arguments rely on verifiable research data rather than personal opinions.

bank.prompt: Which statement is a debatable claim for an argument essay?
choices: Cities should build more protected bike lanes
Bicycles have two wheels and pedals
Columbus is the capital of Ohio
Water freezes at zero degrees Celsius
bank.answer: Cities should build more protected bike lanes
bank.explanation: A claim is a debatable position on an issue that must be proved with evidence.

bank.passage: Buy SolarMax shoes today because millions of fans already wear them!
bank.prompt: Which logical fallacy does this advertisement use?
choices: Bandwagon appeal
Scientific data
Expert medical advice
Historical timeline
bank.answer: Bandwagon appeal
bank.explanation: A bandwagon fallacy claims something is good simply because many other people are doing it.

bank.prompt: Why should an argument essay include a counterclaim?
choices: To address and refute an opposing viewpoint
To confuse the reader about the topic
To prove the author’s own claim is wrong
To avoid using any facts
bank.answer: To address and refute an opposing viewpoint
bank.explanation: A counterclaim is an opposing view. Answering it with evidence makes your argument stronger.

bank.prompt: Which statement gives verifiable factual evidence?
choices: Recycling one ton of aluminum saves 14,000 kWh
Aluminum cans are the prettiest containers
Everyone loves sorting bins on Saturday
Plastic is much more boring than glass
bank.answer: Recycling one ton of aluminum saves 14,000 kWh
bank.explanation: Factual evidence can be measured and checked against reliable records or scientific data.

bank.prompt: What is an ad hominem fallacy in an argument?
choices: Attacking a person instead of their evidence
Using a chart from a science lab
Quoting a dictionary definition
Explaining cause and effect
bank.answer: Attacking a person instead of their evidence
bank.explanation: An ad hominem fallacy attacks the speaker’s character instead of answering their reasoning.

bank.prompt: Which source is most credible for a Lake Erie water report?
choices: Water quality data from the Ohio EPA
An anonymous social media rumour
A comic book about sea monsters
A television commercial for soda
bank.answer: Water quality data from the Ohio EPA
bank.explanation: A credible source is trustworthy and backed by scientific measurement or expert research.

bank.prompt: What connects a piece of evidence back to the author’s claim?
choices: Reasoning
Punctuation
Alliteration
Rhyme
bank.answer: Reasoning
bank.explanation: Reasoning explains how and why the facts prove the author’s main claim.

principles.title: Comparing Two Authors’ Presentations of the Same Event
principles.summary: Compare different nonfiction accounts of the same event.

bank.passage: Author A writes a diary entry from a family trapped on a roof in the 1913 Dayton Flood. Author B writes an engineering report on Miami River dam costs.
bank.prompt: How do these two authors present the same Ohio event?
choices: Author A shares personal feelings; Author B gives technical data
Both authors write fictional fairy tales
Author A lists dam costs; Author B writes poetry
Neither author mentions the river flood
bank.answer: Author A shares personal feelings; Author B gives technical data
bank.explanation: Different authors can cover the same event using a personal memoir or an objective technical report.

bank.passage: Article 1 celebrates how the Ohio & Erie Canal lowered grain shipping prices. Article 2 focuses on the hard labor and illnesses of canal diggers.
bank.prompt: Why do these two articles emphasize different facts?
choices: Article 1 focuses on trade; Article 2 focuses on workers
Article 1 is about space travel
Both articles ignore the canal completely
Article 2 says canals were never built
bank.answer: Article 1 focuses on trade; Article 2 focuses on workers
bank.explanation: Authors select facts that match their purpose, such as economic growth versus worker conditions.

bank.prompt: What is a memoir compared to a history encyclopedia entry?
choices: A firsthand personal memory of events
A list of state capitals in order
A fictional story about talking animals
A math formula for area
bank.answer: A firsthand personal memory of events
bank.explanation: A memoir is a firsthand account written from personal memory, while an encyclopedia is a summary.

bank.passage: Writer 1 describes Wilbur and Orville Wright’s bicycle shop tools in Dayton. Writer 2 describes the wind speeds on the beach at Kitty Hawk.
bank.prompt: What does comparing both passages help the reader understand?
choices: Both the invention work in Ohio and the flight test
Why bicycles cannot roll on roads
How steamboats cross the ocean
Why the Wright brothers quit flying
bank.answer: Both the invention work in Ohio and the flight test
bank.explanation: Reading multiple accounts gives a fuller picture by combining different stages and details of an event.

bank.prompt: What is an author’s perspective in informational nonfiction?
choices: The viewpoint or angle the author brings to a topic
The font size printed on the book cover
The number of pages in the glossary
The price of the book at a store
bank.answer: The viewpoint or angle the author brings to a topic
bank.explanation: Perspective is the author’s viewpoint, which shapes which facts they highlight or leave out.

bank.prompt: How does an eyewitness letter differ from a textbook chapter?
choices: A letter captures immediate emotion; a textbook gives broad context
A textbook is written before the event happens
An eyewitness letter is always fictional
They are identical in every sentence
bank.answer: A letter captures immediate emotion; a textbook gives broad context
bank.explanation: Primary letters show one witness’s immediate view, while textbooks combine many sources later.

bank.passage: Biographer A highlights Garrett Morgan’s three-position traffic signal invented in Cleveland. Biographer B highlights his safety hood used to rescue tunnel workers.
bank.prompt: What central idea do both biographies support about Garrett Morgan?
choices: His inventions saved lives and improved public safety
He only painted landscapes in Europe
He refused to share any of his ideas
He lived before cities had roads
bank.answer: His inventions saved lives and improved public safety
bank.explanation: Both authors use different examples to show that Garrett Morgan’s inventions protected public safety.

bank.prompt: When two authors disagree on a cause, what should a reader check?
choices: The quality of evidence each author cites
Which book has a shinier cover
Which author has a shorter last name
Only the first sentence of each text
bank.answer: The quality of evidence each author cites
bank.explanation: Comparing two accounts requires checking which author backs up claims with stronger evidence.

principles.title: Greek/Latin Roots and Pronoun Case & Intensive Pronouns
principles.summary: Apply roots and pronoun conventions accurately.

bank.prompt: The Greek root "chron" means time. What does chronological mean?
choices: Arranged in time order from first to last
Organized by brightness of color
Sorted from heaviest to lightest
Written in secret code
bank.answer: Arranged in time order from first to last
bank.explanation: The root "chron" means time, so chronological order arranges events in the order they happened.

bank.prompt: The Latin root "spect" means to look. What does inspect mean?
choices: To look at something closely and carefully
To throw something across a field
To freeze water into ice cubes
To whisper a secret song
bank.answer: To look at something closely and carefully
bank.explanation: Because "spect" means look or see, to inspect is to examine closely.

bank.prompt: Which sentence uses pronoun case correctly?
choices: The coach gave Priya and me the blueprint.
The coach gave Priya and I the blueprint.
Her and me built the robot.
Between you and I, the test was easy.
bank.answer: The coach gave Priya and me the blueprint.
bank.explanation: Use the objective pronoun "me" when it receives the action of the verb ("gave me").

bank.prompt: Which sentence uses an intensive pronoun for emphasis?
choices: The principal herself welded the stage frame.
He accidentally cut himself slicing bread.
They bought tickets for our family.
She handed the microphone to him.
bank.answer: The principal herself welded the stage frame.
bank.explanation: An intensive pronoun (like "herself") adds emphasis to a noun and can be removed without breaking grammar.

bank.prompt: The Latin root "port" means carry. What does portable mean?
choices: Easy to carry from place to place
Too heavy to lift off the ground
Able to glow in the dark
Made entirely out of stone
bank.answer: Easy to carry from place to place
bank.explanation: "Port" means carry and "-able" means capable of, so portable means easy to carry.

bank.prompt: Which revision fixes the vague pronoun in "Leo told Sam he won"?
choices: Leo told Sam that Sam had won.
He told him that he won.
Telling him, he won the prize.
They told him he won it.
bank.answer: Leo told Sam that Sam had won.
bank.explanation: A vague pronoun is unclear about who it refers to. Replacing "he" with "Sam" fixes the confusion.

bank.prompt: The Latin root "dict" means say. What does predict mean?
choices: To say what will happen beforehand
To carry boxes onto a ship
To measure the heat of water
To draw a map of mountains
bank.answer: To say what will happen beforehand
bank.explanation: "Pre-" means before and "dict" means say, so predict means to declare beforehand.

bank.prompt: Which sentence uses the subjective pronoun case correctly?
choices: Ava and I presented our history project.
Ava and me presented our history project.
Him and I studied ancient Egypt.
Me and her read the chapter.
bank.answer: Ava and I presented our history project.
bank.explanation: Use the subjective pronoun "I" when it acts as the subject performing the verb.
